title: Kingdom of Essex
capsule: Essex (Ēastseaxna Rīce) was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom of the East Saxons covering modern Essex, Middlesex, and part of Hertfordshire, with London long within its orbit; its king-list traditionally begins with Æscwine and runs through Sledd (c.587–604) and his son Sæberht (c.604–616). Under Sæberht the kingdom accepted Christianity around 604 through Kentish overlordship, and Mellitus became the first post-Roman bishop of London, but after Sæberht's death his sons drove out the bishop and the realm reverted to paganism. A second conversion came under Sigeberht the Good (c.653–660), achieved through the mission of St. Cedd sent from Northumbria, though the East Saxons lapsed again during the plague of 664; throughout this period Essex remained a junior power subordinate by turns to the kings of Kent, Northumbria, and Mercia.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core territory is established from Bede and charter evidence; precise early boundaries, particularly vis-à-vis Mercia and Kent, are disputed among scholars.
